#### Headline: coverage at the kill band and at the clinical level (plain whole-tumour coverage; nominal [eroded .. dilated])

The kill band is DERIVED BY FITTING a single clonogenic series in C6 rat glioma (two 1 h exposures; Caballero Navarro 1992, Histol Histopathol 7:347-351) with -log10(survival) = 0.0426 x exposure (half-kill near 7, one log of kill at 23.5 umol*h/L). Single study, one rat line, and not cleanly proportional at the top dose. It is a band, never a line.

The clinically delivered exposure is MEASURED in human resection-cavity FLUID by mass spectrometry (Ohnishi 2022, Brain Sci 12:567, n = 14-15): mean 262 umol*h/L, range 55-651. It is cavity fluid, not tissue, so it is an upper reference for what the approved therapy produces where the wafer sits, not a tissue target and not a bar.

The clinically delivered exposure (262) is about ten times the one-log-kill level (23.5): potency is not the limitation; transport is.

#### Off-target scored geometrically (MEASURE ONLY: no penalty is added to any score)

No maximum tolerated concentration, exposure or dose for normal brain parenchyma exists for any agent in any species (the absence is structural), so mg outside the tumour has nothing to score against. What exists is the PRECISE catheter protocol (Mueller 2011): release point at least 25 mm below the surface, at least 5 mm from the pia, at least 10 mm from the cavity wall or ependyma. **The pial measures use the brain mask. There are NO ventricle labels in the pipeline (MSD labels are background, edema, non-enhancing and enhancing; the mask includes CSF) and no resection cavity (the scans are pre-operative), so the ependymal numbers use an unvalidated intensity proxy and are a sensitivity, not a result.**
